description: Make sound startup permission-safe so starting or playing the game no longer emits autoplay warnings when audio is blocked.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh and reproduce the current startup/play smoke before editing.
Inspect src/audio.ts, src/game.ts, src/ui.tsx, and existing startup/UI tests to understand the Sound button, intro start path, pointer/touch audio activation, and console warning behavior.

Refactor audio startup so the game does not attempt AudioContext resume or media playback from untrusted/synthetic startup paths; only explicit Sound button clicks or browser-trusted pointer/touch gestures should enable sound.
Keep keyboard movement and intro dismissal independent of audio permission, preserve the existing Sound: off/on button contract, and avoid regressing procedural sound/music fallback behavior.
Add or update tests for the audio enable/auto-audio decision logic using DOM-free helpers or mocked audio where practical.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live browser/CDP smoke that starts the game, moves with keyboard, optionally toggles sound via pointer/click, and records console/runtime exceptions or warnings.
acceptance: A live startup/play smoke can dismiss the intro and move the ship with no Runtime.exceptionThrown events and no autoplay AudioContext warnings from normal keyboard-only play.
Explicit Sound button or trusted pointer/touch activation still enables sound when the browser allows it, and blocked playback fails silently with the icon/state remaining accurate.
Keyboard controls, intro focus, touch controls, and existing HUD/shop behavior remain intact.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.

description: Clarify the in-game sound affordance so players understand sound is opt-in and browser-permission dependent.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh and inspect the intro/HUD sound affordance before editing.
Inspect src/ui.tsx, src/styles.css, src/dom.ts, src/audio.ts, and UI tests for the existing Sound button, intro copy, and accessible labels.
Add concise player-facing copy or button state text that explains sound can be enabled intentionally, without crowding the HUD or mobile layout.
Ensure the affordance updates consistently when sound is enabled, disabled, blocked, or unavailable, while preserving current DOM IDs/classes consumed by the runtime.
Add or update tests that assert the sound control renders with accessible labeling and any new status text or helper output.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live smoke at desktop and narrow/mobile viewport sizes to confirm the sound guidance is visible, non-overlapping, and does not interfere with play.
acceptance: Players can tell from the intro/HUD that sound is optional and should be enabled through the Sound control or a trusted tap/click gesture.
The sound affordance remains readable on mobile-sized layouts and does not overlap critical fuel, hull, cargo, shop, or intro content.
Existing Sound button behavior, keyboard controls, intro flow, and live gameplay remain intact with no runtime exceptions.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.
